ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, shareholders, authorized signatories and any person holding 25% or more of the equity interest must be screened against the PRC Ministry of Public Security domestic watchlist, the PBOC and SAMR beneficial-owner information database, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC's SDN List and non-SDN sectoral sanctions, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission and Bureau of Investigation watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including heads of state, senior executive, legislative, judicial, military and security officials, their family members and close associates. Findings trigger risk escalation, a negative-news search, source-of-funds verification, and transaction monitoring for at least 12 months after a PEP designation or sanctions link is identified. Sanctions hits create a refusal and reporting obligation under PRC AML Law (2025).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Independent Declaration System administered by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), accessible through provincial SAMR online service platforms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered Chinese company name must consist of four tiers: (1) administrative division of the proposed registered office; (2) specific trade name; (3) industry or business characteristic corresponding to the approved business scope, such as data center colocation or server hosting; and (4) organizational form, such as Limited Company. The name must be expressed in statutory Chinese characters; Latin letters, Arabic numerals and pinyin are only permitted as supplementary elements in parentheses or in a separate English name and shall not replace the Chinese statutory name. Phonetic transliteration of the Taiwan investor's name is required where the investor does not have a standard Chinese name; no English-only registered name is permitted. Homophonic misleading terms, terms suggesting state sponsorship, and characters identical to well-known trademarks may be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant shall first obtain the written rejection notice and coded reasons through the SAMR national name portal within five working days. To appeal, the applicant must file an administrative reconsideration application with the competent provincial SAMR within 60 days of receiving the written decision, or file an administrative lawsuit with the competent people's court within six months if reconsideration fails. The appeal must include the originally proposed name, a revised four-tier name structure, evidence of the conflicting trademark or registration, and a comparison table demonstrating compliance with the Enterprise Name Registration Measures. SAMR must respond in writing within 15 working days; during the pendency of the appeal, the applicant may reserve a backup name to preserve filing momentum.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox used as the sole registered address is likely to be rejected by tax authorities, SAMR, and banks for the data center colocation industry. Under PRC Company Law and tax administration practice, the registered address must correspond to the actual business premises, supported by a lease agreement, utility bills, property tax proof, on-site server racks, power capacity, and network facilities. For data center colocation leasing, the operating entity must demonstrate real occupation of the leased racks and physical commercial substance; a purely virtual office will not satisfy the bank account opening requirements or the PBOC risk classification process. A managed server-hotel address is permissible only where the company genuinely occupies the rack space; a letterbox-only arrangement is not acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Physical inspection likelihood is high, estimated at 70% within the first 12 months for a data center colocation entity. The inspection checklist includes: (i) verifying the lease agreement and property ownership certificate; (ii) inspecting server racks, power and cooling systems, network equipment, and access logs; (iii) verifying employees, payroll records, and workstations on site; (iv) matching invoices, bank statements, and utility bills with the registered address; (v) confirming that the registered office is not a letterbox; and (vi) checking environmental, fire-safety, and data-security controls. Municipal tax officials and SAMR field inspectors may conduct unannounced visits under PRC administrative supervision powers. Failures can lead to tax de-registration, company listing as a non-subsisting entity, and banking sanctions.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan (R.O.C.) Company Act, Articles 2, 128, 129, 133, 161, 172, 192, 202, and 387; supplemented by the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and the Company Registration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, through the One-Stop Company Registration Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None (no statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Taiwan Company Act). The Company must receive the full subscribed capital in a domestic bank account, evidenced by a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant capital verification report, before registration is filed. A foreign-invested joint venture must also obtain investment approval from MOEA and complete inward remittance through a designated bank; no blocked escrow account is required for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CN_JV_LTD] (THE 'COMPANY'), ADOPTED ON [DATE] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE] BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANY ACT OF TAIWAN. WHEREAS, the shareholders of the Company have adopted the Articles of Incorporation and subscribed to the share capital, and the Board has been duly constituted; and WHEREAS, the statutory incorporation filing requires the Board to authorize the permanent governance, banking, registered office, and officer arrangements of the Company. NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS ADOPTS THE FOLLOWING RESOLUTIONS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND VERIFICATION. RESOLVED, that the authorized and initial paid-in share capital of the Company be fixed at NT$[●], divided into [●] shares of a par value of NT$[●] each, and that the shareholders' subscription schedule be approved as previously presented. The Board directs management to receive the full subscription amounts into a corporate bank account and to engage a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report in the exact amount of the paid-in capital, to be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company shall establish its principal corporate operating account with [Bank Name], [Branch], and that Chairman/Director [Name], General Manager [Name], and Chief Financial Officer [Name] shall each be authorized to sign and execute cheques, wire-transfer instructions, bank account opening forms, and all related agreements. Any two signatures of the three authorized signatories shall be required for each withdrawal, transfer, or security agreement; the banking authority is effective as of the date of this Resolution and remains in force until superseded by a subsequent Board Resolution. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is established at [Full Address, Taiwan], and that the General Manager is authorized to execute, renew, and file a lease or certificate of title, utility invoices, and any letter of consent required by the registry for the registered office. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chairperson of the Board, [Name] is appointed General Manager, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until earlier resignation, removal, or incapacity. The General Manager, together with the Chairperson, is authorized to prepare and file the Company Establishment Registration Application, to execute declarations concerning no commercial crimes, to resolve any registry observations, and to take all necessary steps for the issuance of the Company Registration Certificate. 5. EFFECTIVENESS. RESOLVED, that the foregoing resolutions take effect immediately but that all actions remain subject to and shall not become operative until the Ministry of Economic Affairs has issued the Company Registration Certificate and the unified business number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Investment Approval and Company Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Investment Commission; MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal name-reservation module.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online investment approval and company name reservation application through the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal and the Investment Commission e-service. The application must include the proposed Chinese and English company names, the intended business scope using the Taiwan Standard Industrial Classification code corresponding to ISIC 6209, the joint venture ownership breakdown, the initial paid-in capital amount, the registered office plan, and the proposed director's identification. The Investment Commission will screen foreign investors, including any Mainland China investor source documentation, and may request a company visit or a due-diligence explanation for the proposed capital injection. After approval, the applicant must pay the name reservation fee and confirm that the company name does not conflict with existing registered marks or entities.
required_dossiers: Investment approval application (Form for Foreign Investment Application)
Passport or company registration certificate of each shareholder, legalized and translated where required
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan agent
Proposed Chinese and English company name reservation application
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Shareholding and capital remittance plan
Business scope description mapped to ISIC 6209 and NAICS 518210
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the investment approval is queried or the name reservation is rejected, the applicant may file a written response or a new name application through the portal within 15 calendar days. For investment-related queries, submit supplemental structural, beneficial-ownership, and source-of-funds evidence to the Investment Commission and request an extension of the original 30-calendar-day approval period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles, Organization Meeting, Capital Deposit, and CPA Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan corporate bank; Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant; notary public for required certifications.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After investment approval is issued, the shareholders must execute the Articles of Incorporation and hold an organization meeting to elect the directors and supervisor and to authorize the general manager. The board then adopts the pro-forma resolutions set out in this dossier. A domestic bank account must be opened in the Company's name, and each shareholder must remit the subscribed capital amount into that account by wire transfer. The remittance instruction must state the shareholder name and the purpose 'paid-in capital'. The bank will issue a capital deposit certificate, and a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant must prepare and sign a capital verification report within 15 calendar days after receipt of funds. Any shortfall, mislabeled remittance, or non-compliance must be cured before the registration application is lodged.
required_dossiers: Investment approval letter
Executed Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the organization meeting or shareholders' meeting
Consent to serve from each director, supervisor, and officer
Bank capital deposit certificate
CPA capital verification report
Company seal and director seal specimen card
Share subscription schedule with paid-in capital amounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the capital deposit or the CPA raises a verification qualification, the shareholders must rectify the remittance reference, provide a letter of explanation from the bank, or re-execute the shareholder subscription schedule and re-deposit the funds. If funds were remitted after the 15-day verification window, obtain a fresh CPA capital verification report before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Establishment Registration Filing with MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, One-Stop Company Registration Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Company Establishment Registration Application with the MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs through the One-Stop Company Registration Portal, using the company's electronic certificate or the attorney's authority. The application must attach the executed Articles of Incorporation, the organization meeting minutes, the board resolution, the CPA capital verification report, the bank deposit certificate, the registered office lease or title certificate, the directors' and officers' consent and identification, and the investment approval letter. The registrar will review statutory signatures, the lawfulness of the business scope, the number of directors, the par value structure, and the registered office. After the registration is approved, MOEA will issue the Company Registration Certificate and assign a unified business number. The applicable registration fee shall be paid electronically.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Application, signed by the authorized representative
Certified true copy of Articles of Incorporation
Organization meeting minutes and first board resolution
CPA capital verification report and bank capital deposit certificate
Proof of registered office (lease agreement, title deed, or owner's consent)
Directors', supervisor's, and officers' identification documents and consents
Investment approval letter
Name reservation filing receipt
Electronic registration fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA requires corrections, file an amended application through the same portal within 15 calendar days, attaching a red-lined signature page or a supplementary statement. If the registration is suspended, re-submit the entire package with the original filing fee receipt and request expedited review under Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Uniform Invoice Activation, Bank Account Activation, and Labor Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District National Taxation Bureau; Municipal Bureau of Labor Insurance; corporate bank branch.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Company Registration Certificate is issued, the Company must activate its corporate bank account by presenting the certificate, the company seal, and the directors' authorization. The Company must then register with the District National Taxation Bureau for income tax, business tax, and uniform invoice use, and report the registered office address. The tax authority will activate the electronic invoice registration, and the Company must apply for a safe-printing design for unified invoices if it will invoice customers for colocation services. Simultaneously, the Company must register as an insurance entity with the Taiwan Labor Insurance Bureau and the National Pension Office to enroll employees. Finally, the bank account activation must be linked to the MOEA registration certificate and the unified business number for wire-transaction compliance.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Unified business number tax registration information
Company seal/chop card and authorized signature specimen
Active corporate bank account confirmation
Uniform Invoice application form
Labor insurance unit registration form and employee enrollment list
Lease or ownership proof for tax office address verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority does not activate invoice usage or the bank account cannot be linked, present the original Company Registration Certificate and a company-seal card to the District National Taxation Bureau and bank branch, correct the address or signatory mismatch, and request same-day re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Facility Compliance for Physical Data Center Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Fire Department; Municipal Labor Authority; local environmental protection bureau.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete post-incorporation operating compliance for a physical data center. The Company must file employment work rules with the municipal labor authority if thirty or more employees are hired, establish a labor health and safety management unit under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, and if the data center premises are owned or leased, register the premises with the municipal fire department and secure a Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Certificate. For a colocation-only operation, no separate industrial license is required; however, the building's occupancy permit should be reviewed to verify live floor loading capacity of at least 1,000 kg per square meter in server areas, or as specified by the structural engineer. Standby generator emission sources, if any, must be permitted with the local environmental protection bureau.
required_dossiers: Work rules text and labor/manning chart
Occupational Safety and Health organization registration forms
Fire Safety Equipment Installation and Inspection Certificate
Building Occupancy Permit and structural live-load check report
Standby generator list and emission test reports
Stationary air pollution source operating permit application
Fire safety management plan and drill records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection or work-rules filing is deficient, correct the noted violations, request a re-inspection within 10 business days, and submit an improvement schedule to the municipality. Any non-compliance with generator emission permits must be cured by applying for a stationary source operating permit and conducting emissions testing before commencement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable (no sectoral industrial licensing authority for ISIC 6209 colocation leasing under Taiwan law; building and fire authorities are facility-level, not licensing).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable (no separate industrial operating license for ISIC 6209 data center colocation leasing; general company registration, tax registration, and facility-level fire/building clearance are the only prerequisites).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable (for current colocation leasing scope); for future ground-up data-center construction, the competent authority would be the Taiwan Ministry of Environment and the local environmental protection bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — data center colocation leasing (ISIC 6209) is not a Category I or Category II development activity listed under the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act; therefore no full EIA Report and no Environmental Registration is required solely for the registered business scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable because the business produces no manufacturing, chemical, or process wastewater/VOC streams. If emergency diesel generators are installed, the data center must obtain a stationary air pollution source permit and comply with the Taiwan Air Pollution Control Act, including fugitive emission controls and fuel sulfur-content limits set by the local environmental protection bureau; server cooling water discharge, if any, must comply with wastewater effluent standards applicable to general industrial sources.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operating any physical server room, the Company must secure a Fire Safety Equipment Installation and Inspection Certificate from the local fire department under the Fire Services Act, verify the Building Occupancy Permit and structural live-load design with a registered engineer, install fire alarm and suppression systems per applicable fire codes, and implement Occupational Safety and Health Act compliance, including electrical safety, emergency exits, fire drills, and worker training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan, acting through the five National Taxation Bureaus (Taipei, Kaohsiung, Northern, Central, Southern) and local tax authorities; online official portals: MOF Tax Entry Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw) for tax registrations and filings, and the e-Invoice Integration Service Platform (einvoice.nat.gov.tw) for electronic uniform invoice clearance and validation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested limited company (the relevant Taiwan implementation of a Sino-foreign equity joint venture), the TIN/VAT ID procurement procedure is: 1. The foreign investors obtain investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) under the Foreign Investment Act. 2. The organizer reserves the company name and business scope with MOEA through the Company Registration Information System. 3. The company files incorporation with MOEA under the Company Act; MOEA issues the incorporation certificate and the eight-digit Unified Business Number (UBIN), which is the sole statutory Taiwan taxpayer identification number and VAT registration number for the entity. 4. The company must complete the tax-file registration (tax registration) with the National Taxation Bureau having jurisdiction over the registered business office before commencing taxable activity; the application must include the MOEA incorporation certificate, the entity constitution, foreign investment approval, business premise lease or ownership evidence, and the appointment of a legal representative. 5. The National Taxation Bureau opens the profit-seeking enterprise tax file and confirms the Business Tax and uniform-invoice obligations; the UBIN is simultaneously used for Business Tax, income tax withholding, and customs matters. 6. The company then registers on the e-Invoice Integration Service Platform for electronic uniform invoice issuance and selects the permitted e-invoice scheme. 7. A foreign non-resident enterprise that has no locally incorporated company and no Taiwan fixed place of business does not receive a UBIN; such an enterprise must apply to the National Taxation Bureau for a non-resident enterprise tax-file number for withholding tax purposes before earning Taiwan-source income and, if it makes taxable cross-border digital-service sales in Taiwan, must comply with the Ministry of Finance cross-border e-service registration scheme.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity election; a locally incorporated limited company is automatically a profit-seeking enterprise taxed at the entity level. No pass-through classification is available for a corporate joint venture, and no consolidated group income tax election is available for a single legal entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (VAT) under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For incorporated companies, no turnover threshold applies: tax registration is mandatory from incorporation and commencement of business. For unincorporated businesses, the simplified registration threshold is TWD 80,000 per month in sales of goods or TWD 40,000 per month in sales of services. The statutory VAT headline rate is 5% on taxable gross receipts.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All businesses must issue uniform invoices for every taxable sale. Electronic uniform invoices must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Integration Service Platform using the approved standard XML/JSON API schema after each issuance; the platform performs format validation and records the invoice number. Transmission must occur within the time windows prescribed by the Electronic Invoice Implementation Standards, generally within 48 hours for consumer-facing B2C e-invoices and within 7 days for B2B e-invoices. The API connection requires a government-approved web-server certificate and identity credentials issued by the platform. Taiwan does not apply per-invoice continuous government clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping in the Latin American sense; instead, anti-fraud control is exercised through the platform's central registration of invoice codes and random encrypted serial numbers printed as QR codes on e-invoice records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, goods exported from Taiwan customs territory and services sold for export are zero-rated. For the data-center colocation and bare-metal hosting scope, zero-rating is available only where the colocation service transaction is demonstrably provided to a foreign enterprise, the service is contractually accepted and used wholly outside Taiwan, the servers and equipment are owned by or under the control of the foreign customer, the consideration is denominated in foreign currency and fully repatriated, and no taxable event is attributable to a domestic Taiwan user. If the rack-space leasing, power, cooling, and physical security services are executed at the Taiwan data center, the Ministry of Finance and National Taxation Bureau will generally treat the service as rendered in Taiwan and subject to 5% business tax rather than zero-rated, unless an advance ruling or dual-criteria export service analysis supports offshore use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration form (export entry) filed by the exporter with Taiwan Customs, showing the goods or equipment physically leaving Taiwan
Commercial invoice issued by the JV to the foreign customer
Bill of lading, air waybill, or international cargo receipt evidencing cross-border transport
Inward remittance advice or foreign exchange settlement certificate issued by an authorized bank in Taiwan proving receipt of the export proceeds
Executed colocation/hosting service agreement identifying the foreign buyer, offshore service-use location, payment in foreign currency, and assignment of server asset ownership or control
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Customs and National Taxation Bureau examiners may audit the export declaration, bill of lading, service contract, bank settlement records, and e-invoice history. Failure to substantiate zero-rating with the complete documentation set causes the transaction to be reclassified as domestic taxable supply; the taxpayer must pay the 5% business tax, with statutory interest, and the output tax is clawed back retrospectively. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, an underpayment or fraudulent use of false invoices to obtain zero-rating is punishable by a surcharge of five to fifteen times the amount of tax evaded in addition to collection of the tax. Intentional evasion may be referred for criminal prosecution under the Tax Collection Act, and the assessment period is extended in cases of fraud or omission, allowing tax authorities to reopen filed returns and claw back export zero-rating benefits for prior years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) adoption of audited financial statements and electronic transmission of the adopted annual accounts to the MOEA corporate registration information platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened by June 30 for the fiscal year ended preceding December 31; approved annual accounts must be transmitted within 15 days after shareholder adoption, normally by mid-July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Company Act liability: responsible director subject to a fine of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000, with continuing periodic fines until filing; MOEA may also order cure or pursue administrative dissolution for serious non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax annual settlement return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 through May 31 following the calendar tax year; extension available only for force majeure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 10 percent of tax payable, minimum TWD 1,500; underreporting or evasion may attract a penalty of up to 100 percent of the underpaid tax, plus default interest and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Income Tax return and second-half instalment payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: September 1 through September 30 each year; instalment equals 50 percent of the prior year tax payable and is waived if prior year payable does not exceed TWD 2,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing results in an automatic assessment of the provisional amount plus default interest; any balance is reconciled in the following May settlement return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Tax (value-added sales tax) return and remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly filers must submit by the 15th day of the following month; data-center colocation leasing ordinarily files monthly, with quarterly filing permitted for smaller-volume taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to TWD 4,000 per return; delinquency surcharge of 1 percent per two-day period, capped at 15 percent of unpaid tax; intentional evasion may be penalized up to five times the underpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding and exemption certificate filing and payee distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronic filing to the tax authority by January 31 following the tax year; physical certificates must reach payees by February 10
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of TWD 1,500 per certificate for failure to file or distribute; remittance delay attracts a monthly surcharge of up to 5 percent of tax due; willful failure to withhold carries a penalty of one to three times the un-withheld amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual operating survey of foreign and overseas-Chinese invested enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronic questionnaire issued between March and May each year for the prior calendar year operations; response due within 30 days of issuance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No statutory monetary fine; non-response may trigger heightened review or delay of the company's future foreign-investment applications.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A CPA audit and attestation is mandatory for a non-public Taiwan company whose paid-in capital exceeds TWD 30 million, whose average annual operating revenue in the prior year exceeds TWD 50 million, or whose outstanding bank loans and endorsements exceed TWD 30 million; the CPA must be licensed by the Financial Supervisory Commission and the audit report must accompany the annual tax return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: As a non-public company, the JV may elect either locally endorsed Financial Accounting Standards (local GAAP) under the Business Entity Accounting Act or Taiwan IFRS; accounts are maintained in New Taiwan Dollars with a fiscal year of January 1 to December 31; accounting vouchers are retained at least 5 years and ledgers and financial statements at least 10 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No recurring UBO declaration is currently required for non-public Taiwanese companies because the annual beneficial-ownership filing mechanism under the Company Act remains suspended following the 2018 referendum; however, the JV must maintain an accurate register of members, record all share transfers, and obtain Investment Commission approval for any issuance or transfer of shares to a foreign investor; the internal AML ownership file is refreshed on each transfer given the low-risk colocation profile.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Shareholders and Directors Meeting Minute Book
Accounting ledgers, vouchers, and approved annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 to 4,500 per year for registered office maintenance, corporate secretarial services, and statutory filings in Taipei or New Taipei
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 to 10,000 per year for a CPA statutory audit and tax-return certification; higher if full Taiwan IFRS reporting is adopted

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Ventures are subject to the standard 25% Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) rate, reduced to 20% for Small Low-Profit Enterprises (annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, employees not exceeding 300, and total assets not exceeding RMB 5,000万). The data center colocation leasing activity does not generally qualify for high-tech or encouraged industry preferential rates unless the JV obtains a High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) certificate, in which case the rate is 15%. Additional super deductions are available for R&D expenses (100% additional deduction) and accelerated depreciation for specialized equipment, but standard colocation leasing is not automatically entitled to these benefits. For qualifying small low-profit enterprises, the effective rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million is effectively 5% (25% of the 20% rate on income up to RMB 1 million, and 25% of the 20% rate on income from RMB 1–3 million under the current preferential calculation), and 20% above RMB 3 million up to the threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: 中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表（A类，2017年版，2021年修订版）Form A000000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Type A), filed electronically via the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (e-Tax / 电子税务局); quarterly provisional filing via Form A200000 (企业所得税月（季）度预缴纳税申报表（A类）)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional filings (预缴申报) due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; annual filing (汇算清缴) due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (May 31 for calendar-year taxpayers)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly: 15th day of the first month following each quarter-end. Annual: 5 months following the close of the fiscal year (on or before May 31). Final settlement of tax due (fourth quarter payment) at the time of annual filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A000000 表头 - 纳税人信息
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, taxpayer identification number (统一社会信用代码), registered address, industry classification code (ISIC 6209 / 国民经济行业分类 信息处理和存储支持服务), date of establishment, and enterprise type (中外合资经营企业)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be completed using the JV’s Chinese unified social credit code; non-resident shareholders are not reflected on the entity’s return except in the shareholder information annex if required by the tax bureau

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 表 - 利润总额计算 (Line 1-10)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income: revenue from colocation leasing (服务器托管及机柜租赁收入), rental income from bare-metal servers, cost of sales (data center electricity, cooling, bandwidth, depreciation, staff costs), operating expenses, fair value adjustments, and non-operating income/expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report full gross revenue from Taiwan and other offshore customers sourced within China; no apportionment for non-resident shareholders unless the JV is a permanent establishment of a foreign parent, which is not the case for the standalone Chinese JV

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A105000 表 - 纳税调整项目明细表
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to accounting profit: disallowed expenses (entertainment expenses limited to 60% and 0.5% of revenue), advertising expenses (15% revenue cap), donation caps (30% of annual accounting profit via public welfare channels), depreciation differences, and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any intercompany management fees charged by the Taiwan/JV foreign parent must satisfy the State Administration of Taxation (SAT) beneficial ownership and substance requirements; non-arm’s-length fee adjustments must be reflected here

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A107010 / A107012 表 - 免税、减计收入及加计扣除优惠明细表
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax incentives: R&D super deduction, accelerated depreciation for dedicated data center equipment (if selected), income from qualified technical services, and investment tax credits if applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Colocation leasing is generally a service/rental activity; none of the automatic exemptions apply. If the JV holds software copyrights and derives software product income, the 'two-year exemption, three-year half rate' software enterprise incentive may apply upon registration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A106000 表 - 企业所得税弥补亏损明细表
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of loss carryforwards: prior-year taxable losses are carried forward and offset against current-year taxable income; the carryforward period is 10 years for losses incurred in 2018 and after; for losses incurred before 2018, the period is 5 years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special non-resident limitation; the JV’s own operating losses must be domestically sourced and supported by audited financial statements

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A108000 表 - 境外所得抵免明细表
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit schedule: if the JV has income sourced from Taiwan or other jurisdictions and has paid foreign income tax, the credit is computed on a country-by-country basis with a 5-year carryforward of excess credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income from leasing server racks to Taiwan-based customers is generally sourced in China where the servers are physically located, regardless of customer location; therefore no foreign tax credit is typically available

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A109000 表 - 跨地区经营汇总纳税企业年度分摊表
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable only if the JV operates branch data centers in multiple Chinese provinces; head office must perform allocation and file the branch-specific schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the JV has only a single registered establishment in China, this schedule is not required; for cross-province branch expansion, the 50% / 50% allocation rule between head office and branches applies

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: RMB 2,000 for the first late filing, increasing to RMB 2,000–10,000 for repeated non-compliance; daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% (万分之五) per day on any unpaid tax balance, accruing from the statutory deadline to the date of actual payment. For underreporting/deficiency caused by fraud or false filing, penalty is 50% to 5 times the tax evaded, plus possible criminal liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by a Chinese-resident enterprise to its non-resident corporate shareholder under the Enterprise Income Tax Law Art. 3 and 37; a 5% preferential rate applies if the foreign shareholder is a qualifying resident of a treaty/jurisdiction with a 5% reduced dividend withholding provision (e.g., Hong Kong SAR or Singapore under certain conditions), subject to the holding period and beneficial ownership requirements. Taiwan is treated as a domestic jurisdiction for many cross-strait matters in practice, but the cross-strait tax treaty (海峡两岸避免双重征税及加强税务合作协议) is limited in scope and has no statutory dividend withholding reduction to 5%; therefore the standard 10% rate applies for repatriation to Taiwanese shareholders unless the shareholder operates through a Hong Kong/Singapore intermediate holding company that meets the treaty's principal purpose and substance tests. The Taiwan shareholder may also be taxed in Taiwan on the dividend, with a foreign tax credit for the 10% Chinese WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief: (1) the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Resident Certificate (TRC, 税收居民证明) from the competent tax authority of its residence jurisdiction; (2) before the payment date, the shareholder submits Form A03094 (非居民纳税人享受税收协定待遇情况报告表) or files the withholding tax reduction application via the Chinese payer's e-Tax system, providing the TRC, shareholder structure chart, ownership records for the 12-month continuous holding period (if applying the 5% direct investment rate), and substantive business documentation (place of effective management, employees, and business premises in the residence jurisdiction); (3) the Chinese payer withholds at the reduced rate only after the tax bureau issues an acknowledgment; (4) for the 10% standard rate on treaty or non-treaty dividends, no formal pre-approval is required—the withholding agent (the JV) must withhold and remit within 7 days of the dividend resolution; (5) the tax bureau may conduct post-payment anti-abuse examination under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the principal purpose test (PPT) contained in the multilateral instrument where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 10% on royalties and interest payments to non-residents that are not attributable to a Chinese permanent establishment. Treaty-reduced rates: under the Hong Kong/Singapore DTA, interest is typically 7–10% (with some cases of exemption for financial institutions), royalties 5–7%, and dividends 5% for qualifying substantial holdings; under the Taiwan cross-strait arrangement, the agreed rates replicate the standard 10% statutory cap generally without favorable reduction to 5%. Royalties paid for the use of software, IP, or patented data center technology are subject to WHT at 10% (or 5–7% under a DTA), and are subject to VAT on the payment at 6% (with VAT WHT by the payer for non-residents). Interest paid on shareholder loans from Taiwan to the Chinese JV is subject to 10% WHT plus VAT at 6% unless the loan is at or below the arm’s length thin capitalization safe harbor threshold (2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial enterprises). Where the lender is a Taiwan bank, the rate may be reduced under treaty practice only if the cross-strait arrangement includes such financial interest provisions; in practice, the standard 10% plus business tax is applied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous Local File threshold: annual related-party transactions exceeding RMB 10 million for tangible property purchases/sales, or exceeding RMB 40 million in total for all other related-party transactions (including services, interest, and royalties); Master File threshold: annual controlled transactions exceeding RMB 1 billion in aggregate or the entity is a member of a group whose annual related-party revenue exceeds RMB 1 billion and that is one of the largest 100 worldwide; Special Factor File (特殊事项文档) required for intangible property transactions exceeding RMB 10 million. The Taiwan–China JV is presumed to have cross-border related-party transactions (management fees, technical service fees, colocation revenue from affiliated Taiwan data center clients) and must perform an annual related-party transaction disclosure (年度关联业务往来报告表, Form A/J/S) with the EIT return, including the Local File disclosure if the thresholds are met.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price), Resale Price Method, Cost Plus Method, TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method), Profit Split Method
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as codified in Taiwan’s Anti-Hybrid Mismatch and controlled foreign corporation rules are not directly applicable to the PRC-jurisdiction JV; however, the Chinese tax administration applies the multifactor substance analysis under SAT Public Notice No. 7 (2015) and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) in EIT Law Art. 47: the JV must demonstrate real business purpose, actual management and decision-making in China, sufficient employees (headcount), tangible data center assets (servers, racks, power infrastructure), and risk-bearing capacity. If the Taiwan shareholder receives passive income (dividends, royalties, interest) without economic substance, the Chinese payer may deny treaty benefits, recharacterize the income, and impose 10% WHT plus late surcharges; the Taiwanese shareholder may also be subject to Taiwan’s CFC rules if the JV is classified as a CFC and its income is predominantly passive under Taiwan's Income Tax Act Art. 43-4.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (偷税) and Fraudulent Tax Refund
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of colocation lease revenue, fabrication of invoices (虚开发票) for electricity or bandwidth costs, concealment of Taiwan-related related-party revenue, use of shell intermediary companies to divert rental income, or claiming false EIT losses/incentives without statutory basis
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SAT will assess back taxes, impose a surcharge of 0.05% per day on the unpaid amount, and impose a penalty of 50% to 5 times the evaded tax; criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201 (tax evasion) where the amount is over RMB 100,000 and constitutes 10% or more of the total taxable income, punishable by up to 7 years imprisonment and unlimited fines; conviction triggers de facto corporate debarment from public procurement and cross-border bank credit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under EIT Law Art. 49 and SAT anti-evasion practice, directors and de facto controllers (including the Taiwan-appointed director) can be jointly and severally liable for restitution of the evaded tax if they authorized, signed, or knowingly benefited from the false filing; travel bans (限制出境) under the Tax Collection Law Art. 44 and 52 can be imposed by SAT for unpaid tax above RMB 20,000; imprisonment up to 7 years, plus prohibition from serving as a director of any PRC company for up to 5 years after criminal conviction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Shifting taxable profits out of China by paying inflated management fees, above-market royalties for non-existent IP licenses, artificially high interest on shareholder loans, or underpricing colocation rack rental charged to affiliated Taiwan data center customers to erode the Chinese JV taxable base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SAT may re-assess taxable income under the arm’s length principle and impose a transfer pricing penalty of 5% to 20% of the under-assessed tax (Public Notice No. 16, 2018) if no contemporaneous documentation was prepared; with documentation, only late payment interest applies (base rate plus 2 percentage points); back-adjustments for up to 10 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign inflated TP documentation or false related-party transaction schedules face joint and several liability for the re-assessed tax if the entity becomes insolvent; they are also subject to personal fines up to RMB 500,000 under the criminal law for providing false financial statements; travel bans and non-liability release are not available until the reassessment is paid

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance and Tax Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the JV as a pass-through shell with no employees in China, with servers actually owned and operated by a Taiwan affiliate, or inserting a Hong Kong/Singapore conduit company that lacks business substance solely to reduce dividend/royalty WHT from 10% to 5% under a DTA without satisfying the beneficial ownership requirement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the PPT and beneficial ownership rules, recharacterization of income with full 10% WHT, additional 50% to 3 times WHT penalty for failure to withhold (public notice 372, 2016); Taiwan’s taxpayer may be imputed CFC income under Taiwan Income Tax Act Art. 43-4, triggering Taiwan EIT at 20% with credit for Chinese WHT; the PRC JV may be deemed non-tax-compliant leading to a tax compliance classification downgrade (失信) with public credit blacklisting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the shell JV (including the Taiwan nominator) are jointly liable for uncollected withholding tax if the JV failed to withhold dividends/royalties; they can be prohibited from exiting Chinese mainland territory under Art. 6 of the Exit-Entry Administration Law, and may face criminal liability under Art. 205 if the shell is used for invoice fraud; Taiwan CFC regime can attribute undistributed earnings to the individual Taiwan controlling shareholder subject to a 5% surcharge for failure to report

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Foreign Exchange Control Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing of colocation lease rental payments through non-operational offshore accounts, undertaking cross-border payments to Taiwan suppliers without a customs/foreign exchange declaration, retaining rental income outside China without submitting foreign exchange settlement, or circumventing SAFE verification thresholds by splitting payments monthly despite the actual transaction being a bundled cross-border service
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2023), a corporate fine of up to RMB 5 million for serious non-compliance and suspension of business; under the Provisional Regulations on Foreign Exchange Control Art. 39, a fine of 30% to 5 times the foreign exchange amount for illegal cross-border transfer; SAFE may blacklist the JV and revoke its settlement eligibility
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally direct the offshore cash routing face personal criminal liability under the PRC Criminal Law Art. 190 (foreign exchange evasion) and Art. 191 (money laundering), with imprisonment of 5 to 10 years and personal fines of up to RMB 5 million; in addition, under the Tax Collection Law Art. 44, the SAT can restrict exit and revoke passports; bank account freeze orders against directors’ personal Taiwan and China accounts are available to enforce restitution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Invoicing (虚开增值税发票) and VAT Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing false VAT special invoices to downstream tenants for colocation space, overstating input VAT via fake electricity utility invoices from unlicensed third-party energy sellers, or using a third-party platform to split rent into an artificial service fee to escape VAT or to supply invoices to tenants as a means of improper deduction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT penalty of up to 50% of the tax amount plus daily surcharge; criminal conviction for false invoice issuance under PRC Criminal Law Art. 205 imposes a fine of RMB 50,000 to 500,000 on the entity and imprisonment of the responsible individuals for up to 15 years; the tax authority concurrently revokes qualification for simplified tax treatment and denies credit for all connected invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, financial director, and Taiwan-nominated senior manager who sign or authorize invoice issuance are individually subject to criminal liability even where the entity is dissolved (Art. 205, Criminal Law); they are barred from leaving China, and their personal assets are attachable for VAT restitution under civil restitution rules
